name: Rome
startIntroPart1: First among equals, Augustus Caesar claims his right. You, who never call yourself Emperor, are revered by your people as a god. The world now is disorder; you will give it form. The world is leaderless; you will provide it direction. Set the laurels on your head and issue your commands - lead your people to glory, and your name will become synonymous with rule.
startIntroPart2: Rome: a name synonymous with power. Legend has it that the first Romans were raised by wolves. Seeing the debates in the Senate, the achingly straight Roman roads, and the well-ordered legions, one might doubt this. Seeing the light of ambition in Roman eyes, one does not. Raise the eagle standard, and let the world know the glory that is Rome.
attacked: Come, break your swords on our walls.
defeated: Have I played the part well? Then, I exit.
introduction: I am Octavian, Augustus Caesar, a simple first citizen. And emperor of the world.

name: America
startIntroPart1: Writer, printer, and inventor, you offer your counsel to all who ask - and many who do not. With your dry wit and keen mind, you challenge the injustice of foreign rule and set your inventive mind towards building a nation based on principled rationality. Benjamin Franklin, bring your sound advice, and let us ensure that the sun rises on your people.
startIntroPart2: Built on steam, on iron, and on a vision that looks relentlessly ahead, America surges forward. The brave new world unrolls from factory assembly lines, on rail tracks that extend across the plains, and in the eyes of each immigrant who sets foot upon its shores. Come, and dream anew, under the stars and stripes.
declaringWar: War is always tragedy, the more so that you have forced our hand into this.
attacked: So you would waste all the industry of your people on death.
defeated: What use are tools without a project? Of what use is a mind without ideas? I shall set these down and move on.
introduction: Greetings! I am Benjamin Franklin, doctor, scientist, writer, and full of advice, whether you will listen or not.

name: Egypt
startIntroPart1: Great Pharaoh Hatshepsut, your name is written again and again in immortal stone. Extend your hand now, and bring once again wonders from the sand. Ensure that your people, like the river, rise and fall, but never vanish.
startIntroPart2: From the river-fed fields of grain to the polished limestone obelisks rises Egypt. Nurtured by the black soil that graces its riverbanks, Egypt provides for its people. And in its limestone obelisks and tombs, it challenges the most implacable of foes – time itself. Take up now the sharpened khopesh or the bronze chisel and make your mark - immortality awaits.
declaringWar: When we are done, the lone and level sands will be all that remains of you.
attacked: The nau-snake is in my belly, and I have not given myself to you, your flame will not be on me.
defeated: Open the Netherworld so that I may see my father Osiris and drive away darkness, for I am beloved of him. All you spirits, prepare a path for me.
introduction: I am Horus in human flesh — Hatshepsut, pharaoh of the red lands and the black lands.

name: Maurya
startIntroPart1: Chakravartin Ashoka, the wheel-turning monarch, your success in war made plain to you its costs. Determined to end the cycle of violence that marked your time as emperor of Maurya, you brought wisdom instead of swords, the dharma in place of destruction, and a message of non-violence to all beings. The world now needs your wisdom.
startIntroPart2: Maurya life thrums to the thud of ox hoofs returning from the fields, the clatter of palm-leaf texts, the beat of the bhambha drums, the steady rhythm of monks’ chants, the whisper of court attendants. Lend your voice, lead the song.
declaringWar: The path of violence is a path that I swore never to take again. But here we are.
attacked: Violence echoes across multiple lives, multiple worlds. It will return to you.
defeated: And now, the burning wheel passes over me.
introduction: I am Ashoka, the great king at the center of the world, and profound sinner.

name: Songhai
startIntroPart1: Amina, sarauniya of the Hausa, bowing to none, prepare your mount for war. You who would not serve, protected those who served you behind high walls - and rode down those who would not. Fight now, sarauniya, and gain what is yours.
startIntroPart2: Masters of the rivers and desert alike, the Songhai venture forth into the land. Stirred by the songs of the griot, and driven by their passion for profit and God alike, they seek out the riches of the world. Ride now with them, whether driven on by ambition or virtue, and lay claim to what you can.
declaringWar: As we devour your cities with war, we will open the gates, and let the hyenas break your bones.
attacked: Our blades are sharp. Your necks are soft.
defeated: From obscurity I rose, and to it I must return. From the desert I will watch you.
introduction: I am Amina, Sarauniya and taker of whatever — and whomever — pleases me.

name: The Han
startIntroPart1: Master Kong, you gave guidance to rulers when they were lost. Now, wise one, the world is again in need of your guidance. Help us to temper duty with benevolence; help us to see with wisdom and propriety. Where the darkness of ignorance falls, lead us in the righteous path.
startIntroPart2: Forged from the legacies of the militaristic Qin and the cultured Zhou, the Han Dynasty of China rules with righteousness tempered with benevolence, with wisdom informed by tradition. Han engineers transformed the land, even as Han philosophers transformed the mind. Go now, and take up the Mandate of Heaven.
declaringWar: One must know when one can fight. And now we can.
attacked: Heaven is against you. you shall see.
defeated: Death! What a blessing! The righteous man can rest, and villains' tricks end.
introduction: Have you come to me, Kong Fu Zi, seeking knowledge? That already is knowledge.
